The field limit_window_seconds goes through flexibleDoubleIfPresent (OpenAIWireTypes.swift:76, AppConfig.swift:199-203). That helper only runs try? decodeIfPresent(Double.self), with no range or isFinite check, so 1e300 arrives as a finite Double. toSnapshot/window() (OpenAIWireTypes.swift:143-145) calls kind.label(from:) whenever used_percent is present. humanLabel (OpenAIWireTypes.swift:207) only checks `s > 0`. Lines 211 and 213 then run `Int(days.rounded())` / `Int(hours.rounded())`. In Swift, Int(Double) on an out-of-range value is a runtime trap. A trap is not a thrown error, so no try?/catch further up (CachedFetch, provider) can catch it. There is no clamp, no Int(exactly:), and no type-system barrier. The only real limiter is the threat model: the attacker has to control the vendor response itself, since the host is fixed and TLS protects it. That limits severity (LOW, DoS of a local app).
